# Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement

## Problem statement

The repository contains only documentation (`docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md`, worklog tooling) — no game code exists yet. The operator wants the first gym scene: a self-contained Phaser scene with only the player ship and space-style thrust movement (Asteroids-like physics with momentum and inertia, wrapped screen edges). This will establish the project scaffold and serve as a testbed for core gameplay mechanics.

## Users

- **Player / developer** testing the game — wants to fly the ship in a bare scene to verify the movement model feels right before any gameplay is added.
- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — need a runnable Phaser scene + a well-defined, testable movement model as the foundation for all later mechanics.

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want to steer a neon ship with the arrow/WASD keys so I can get used to its drifting, momentum-based movement.
- As a **player**, I want to be able to fly off any screen edge and reappear on the opposite side, so the scene has no hard walls.
- As a **developer**, I want the movement physics implemented as a small, testable unit (pure Newtonian model), so I can tune constants and add tests without Phaser coupling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Project bootstrapped (dependency):** The block "Bootstrap Phaser + TypeScript project scaffold (AH-0MT97OA3E001DOYW)" is complete; this scene builds and runs on top of it.
- [ ] **AC2 — Gym scene with only the player ship:** A `Gym.ts` scene (Phaser scene registered in the game config) renders exactly one entity — the player ship. No enemies, no bullets (no firing at all), no HUD, no power-ups, no background gameplay.
- [ ] **AC3 — Thrust-based movement input:** W/A/S/D and Arrow Up/Down/Left/Right apply thrust acceleration in that direction (diagonals supported when two perpendicular keys are held simultaneously). All eight directions are usable.
- [ ] **AC4 — Newtonian drift (pure space movement):** Movement is pure Newtonian — zero friction, zero damping. Velocity changes only via thrust: pressing a direction accelerates the ship in that direction; releasing keys preserves current velocity (drift); stopping/reversing requires opposite thrust. An absolute speed cap (max speed) prevents unbounded acceleration, per the "Asteroids-like" model.
- [ ] **AC5 — Feels responsive, not sluggish:** Thrust/max-speed constants are tuned so the ship reaches meaningful speed quickly and decelerates/reverses within a "short moment" of holding the opposite key. Tuning constants (thrust, max speed) are exposed in one place (e.g., a config/constants module) so the feel is adjustable without digging through scene code.
- [ ] **AC6 — Screen edge wrap-around:** The ship wraps across all four screen edges (leaves left, reappears right, etc.) rather than being clamped, matching the operator's choice (Asteroids-style).
- [ ] **AC7 — GDD updated:** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.2 Movement is updated to describe the thrust-based, Newtonian-drift model (zero friction, max speed, wrap-around edges) replacing the current "movement speed is constant" wording. §2.1 controls wording ("Move up/down/left/right") remains consistent with thrust semantics.
- [ ] **AC8 — Testing/validation:** The movement model is unit-tested (e.g., Vitest): thrust applies acceleration in the correct direction, diagonal thrust combines correctly, zero-friction drift preserves velocity when keys are released, opposite thrust reduces/reverses velocity, max-speed cap applies, and wrap-around math is correct. All tests pass.
- [ ] **AC9 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC10 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine:** Phaser v4 (locked, GDD §6.2) + TypeScript; code-first (no visual editor). Must satisfy web + Windows binary constraints (GDD §6.3).
- **Gym scene scope is intentionally minimal:** exactly one scene containing only the player ship + movement; no firing, no auto-fire, no enemies, no HUD, no lives/score. Auto-fire, collisions, and other mechanics belong to later work items, not this one.
- **Movement model:** pure Newtonian (zero friction/damping), acceleration via thrust, max-speed cap, wrap-around screen edges (operator decisions Q2/Q3).
- **Player ship visuals:** neon-vector aesthetic per GDD §7.1; ship is the cyan (`#00ffff`) small angular shape (e.g., triangle/chevron) per §2.3/§4.1 styling. Should be drawn/represented in code (no external art assets required for the gym — placeholder acceptable).
- **Thruster feedback:** pressing a direction key should visually indicate thrusters firing (e.g., a small flame/glow opposite the thrust direction) so movement input is legible without racing the physics. (Simple visual acceptable; no particles system required.)
- **GDD §2.2 must be updated** as part of this item (operator decision Q1).

## Existing state

- No game code exists in the repo; `docs/Game Design Document.md` and `README.md` are the only content besides worklog tooling.
- GDD §2.2 currently reads: "Movement speed is constant; acceleration and deceleration are smooth but responsive." — to be replaced by the thrust/drift model.
- GDD §2.1 controls table: W/A/S/D + arrows = move up/down/left/right; autofire is continuous (out of scope here).
- GDD §6.4 proposes `src/entities/Player.ts` and electron module layout; `Player.ts` interface (§6.5) lists `speed`, `fireRate` etc.
- README.md describes this exact gym-scene intake as the first implementation step.

## Desired change

1. Bootstrap the project (separate work item AH-0MT97OA3E001DOYW, this item depends on it).
2. Add a `Gym.ts` Phaser scene rendering only the player ship (neon triangle/chevron, cyan).
3. Implement movement as pure Newtonian physics: directional thrust (WASD/arrows, diagonals), zero-friction drift, max-speed cap, screen wrap.
4. Show thruster flames while a direction key is held.
5. Update GDD §2.2 with the new movement model.
6. Unit-test the movement model (acceleration, drift, reverse, cap, wrap).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, Vite config, `index.html` — from the bootstrap item (dependency).
- `src/scenes/Gym.ts` (or `src/gym/Gym.ts` per GDD §6.4 layout) — the gym scene.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — player ship entity with movement model (GDD §6.4/§6.5).
- `src/utils/movement.ts` / `src/core/` — pure movement/physics math unit under test.
- `src/config/` (or similar) — tunable movement constants (thrust, max speed).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §2.2 movement section update.

## Related work

- **Bootstrap Phaser + TypeScript project scaffold (AH-0MT97OA3E001DOYW)** — blocking dependency (this item depends on the scaffold existing).
- Game Design Document for AI_Hell (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5) — parent epic; GDD is the authoritative spec, §2.2 updated here.
- GDD revision items (AH-0MT7UTPH3001B6IE engine lock, AH-0MT7UW0Y80062NU1 audio in scope, etc.) — context; the GDD §2.2 edit must not conflict with them.
- README.md — documents this gym scene as the first implementation step.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — feel tuning is subjective:** "not sluggish, but forces thinking ahead" is a qualitative target. Mitigation: expose constants (thrust, max speed) in one config module; unit tests lock the math, manual playtest tunes values; record target feel params (e.g., time to reach max speed, time to reverse) in the GDD §2.2 update so the tuning is auditable.
- **Risk — bootstrap churn:** the scaffold (Vite/TS/Phaser versions) may change while the dependency is implemented. Mitigation: implement against a stable Phaser v4 + Vite + TypeScript baseline; this item is blocked on bootstrap completion, per the dependency edge.
- **Assumption — no ship rotation:** the ship is a static neon shape oriented "up"; thrust is applied in key directions rather than a rotating ship (Asteroids-style rotation is not requested and out of scope; movement feel comes from physics, not orientation).
- **Assumption — wrap-around position only:** velocity is unchanged when crossing an edge; the ship simply reappears on the opposite side.
- **Assumption — no firing/autofire in the gym:** the scene contains "nothing but the player ship"; combat mechanics are later work items.
- **Scope-creep guard:** particles, screen-shake, collision, enemies, HUD, pause, and audio are explicitly out of scope for the gym; record any extras as linked work items, not this one.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should this item also update the GDD §2.2 movement spec to match the new thrust/drift model, or leave the GDD untouched for now?" — Answer (user): **"Update"** — §2.2 is updated as part of this item. Source: interactive reply (round 1). Final accepted: GDD §2.2 rewritten to describe thrust-based Newtonian drift, max speed, wrap-around edges.
- Q2: "Physics model — (a) pure Newtonian zero-friction (classic Asteroids), or (b) very light friction so the ship coasts to a stop when no keys are held?" — Answer (user): **"a"** — pure Newtonian, zero friction; velocity changes only via thrust; stopping requires reverse thrust. Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q3: "Screen-edge behavior — clamp within screen bounds, or wrap-around like classic Asteroids?" — Answer (user): **"wrap"** — the ship wraps across all four screen edges. Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q4: "Should project bootstrap (package.json, TS config, build tooling) be part of this item or separate?" — Answer (user): **"Create a separate work item to bootstrap. Make the player scene dependent upon the bootstrap."** — bootstrap is a separate work item (AH-0MT97OA3E001DOYW) with a dependency edge gym→bootstrap. Source: interactive reply (round 1).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5** – Game Design Document for AI_Hell (completed)
- **AH-0MT7QQGBU008V4R0** – Write the Game Design Document (completed)

# Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (epic)

## Problem statement

The first three enemy gym scenes — E1 Scout (`GymScout.ts`), E2 Diver (`GymDiver.ts`), E3 Tank (`GymTank.ts`) — were built independently and share ~90% identical structure: formation spawn loop, EXPLODE/SHOOT HUD buttons, status text, hint line, back-to-index button, formation drift + respawn logic, per-entity `applyFormationPosition` update, bullet collection/advance/off-screen removal, `_bulletOffScreen`, `_respawnX`, and the `labelStyle`/`_addButton` UI helpers. Only the entity type, formation-offset builder, constants, fire method (`tryFireAimedBullet` / `tryFireSpreadBurst` / `tryFireRadialBurst`), status label and hint text differ.

This epic extracts that duplicated behaviour into a reusable core library, rewrites each gym scene to consume it, documents best practice for building enemy gym scenes, and brings the remaining enemy-gym-scene work items (E4 Phaser, E5 Swarm, Boss) into line with those best practices.

## Users

- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — want one well-tested place for formation scenes so new enemy gym scenes (E4/E5/Boss) are thin, focused scene classes instead of another near-copy of the same 200-line boilerplate.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want a shared gym formation-scene base class that encapsulates spawn/UI/update/bullet lifecycle, so each new enemy gym scene supplies only its entity-specific config.

# Gym index scene

## Problem statement

The project now has multiple gym scenes (player movement + enemy testbeds) but no way to reach them: `gameConfig.ts` hard-codes a single scene, so each scene can only be tested by editing source. Developers need a gym entry page that automatically lists every available gym scene, booted first in dev mode, so individual scenes can be selected and tested in isolation without touching code.

## Users

- **AI agents / developers implementing AI_Hell** — want to boot the project, see every gym scene listed, click one to test it in isolation, and return to the list; adding a new gym scene must not require editing the index.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want to start the app with `npm run dev` (or `npm run preview`) and land on a gym index that lists all gym scenes sorted alphabetically, so I can pick what to test.
- As a **developer**, I want the scene list to be discovered from `src/scenes/gym/` rather than hard-coded, so a newly added `GymDiver.ts` appears automatically without editing the index.
- As a **developer**, I want entries labelled from their filename (e.g. `Scout`, `Tank`, `Player`) and, on selection, to jump straight into that scene.
- As a **developer**, I want a "← INDEX" button in every gym scene so I can return to the index without reloading the page.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Player gym scene relocated & renamed:** `src/scenes/Gym.ts` (class `GymScene`) moves to `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` as class `GymPlayer` (key `GymPlayer`), consistent with the `GymScout` / `GymTank` convention; all references (game config, tests, docs) are updated and the build/typecheck passes.
- [ ] **AC2 — Gym index entry scene:** A new `GymIndex` scene is the sole scene registered in `gameConfig.ts`; running `npm run dev` or `npm run preview` boots into the index, which shows a title and the alphabetical list of discovered gym scenes.
- [ ] **AC3 — Directory-dynamic discovery (no hard-coded list):** The index enumerates gym scenes by reading `src/scenes/gym/` via Vite's `import.meta.glob` — no explicit scene array. `.test.ts` files are excluded from the list, and the index itself is not listed (it lives outside the glob folder). Adding a new `Gym<Name>.ts` file to the folder makes it appear without editing the index.
- [ ] **AC4 — Display names, sorting & immediate switching:** Labels are the filename with the leading `Gym` stripped (`GymScout` → `Scout`, `GymPlayer` → `Player`) and sorted alphabetically; selecting an entry immediately starts that scene using its class-name key.
- [ ] **AC5 — Back-to-index button:** Every gym scene (existing `GymScout` / `GymTank` updated, `GymPlayer` included, convention documented for future scenes) shows a small "← INDEX" button that switches back to `GymIndex`.
- [ ] **AC6 — Testing/validation:** Unit tests cover discovery filtering (`.test.ts` excluded), display-name derivation, alphabetical sorting, and scene switching; player-scene tests are updated for the rename; full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README (dev-run instructions + "adding a new gym scene" convention), and the GDD layout notes.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript + Vite (already pinned in `package.json`). Discovery must use Vite's `import.meta.glob` (works in dev server, `vite preview`, and Vitest) — browsers cannot read the filesystem at runtime.
- **Discovery is data-driven:** the index enumerates scenes from the folder contents; no scene-registry edit is required when a gym scene is added.
- **Dev-mode entry:** the index is the entry page when the server runs via `npm run dev` / `npm run preview`, per the operator. No production game scene exists yet, so the index is the single entry point for all run modes at this stage.
- **Naming conventions:** gym scenes live in `src/scenes/gym/` as `Gym<Name>.ts` with class/key `Gym<Name>`; labels strip the `Gym` prefix; the index scene lives outside the folder (e.g. `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts`) so it is naturally excluded from discovery.
- **Aesthetic:** neon-vector, dark background, monospace UI text in the index (consistent with the existing gym HUD buttons — see `GymScout.ts` label style and GDD §7.1 / §2.3).
- **Back-to-index:** implemented once as a shared helper and applied to all gym scenes (existing and new), keeping scenes consistent.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/Gym.ts` — player movement gym scene, class/key `GymScene`; registered in `gameConfig.ts` as the only scene.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymScout.ts`, `GymTank.ts`, `GymDiver.ts` (each + `.test.ts`) — enemy gym scenes with in-scene HUD buttons (`EXPLODE`, `SHOOT: ON/OFF`), monospace text style.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymScout.ts` etc. do not currently know about the index; there is no navigation between scenes.
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — `scene: [GymScene]`.
- `src/main.ts` → `core/Game.ts` → `buildGameConfig()` — the boot path.
- GDD §6.4 proposes `src/ui/Menu.ts` ("Main menu, game-over screen") for the shipped game — distinct from this dev-only gym index.
- `README.md` documents the first gym-scene intake as the implementation start; no gym-index documentation yet.

## Desired change

1. Move and rename the player gym scene: `src/scenes/Gym.ts` → `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts`, class/key `GymScene` → `GymPlayer`; update `gameConfig.ts`, tests, and any references.
2. Add `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — entry scene that discovers gym scenes from `src/scenes/gym/` via `import.meta.glob`, filters `.test.ts` files, derives labels (strip `Gym`), sorts alphabetically, and lists them as clickable entries.
3. Register `GymIndex` in `gameConfig.ts` as the entry scene so `npm run dev` / `npm run preview` boot into it.
4. Selecting an entry immediately starts that scene by its class-name key (`this.scene.start('Gym<Name>')`).
5. Add a shared "← INDEX" back-button helper and apply it to `GymScout`, `GymTank`, and `GymPlayer`.
6. Document the convention in README/GDD and unit-test the discovery/derivation/sort/switching logic.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — NEW: index/entry scene (title, discovered scene list, immediate switching).
- `src/scenes/gym/discovery.ts` (or `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`) — NEW: Vite `import.meta.glob` discovery, `.test.ts` filtering, display-name derivation, alphabetical sort; pure, unit-testable.
- `src/utils/gymNavigation.ts` — NEW: shared "← INDEX" back-button helper used by all gym scenes.
- `src/scenes/Gym.ts` → moved to `src/scenes/gym/GymPlayer.ts` — renamed player gym scene (class/key `GymPlayer`).
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — register `GymIndex` as the entry scene (replacing `GymScene`).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymScout.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymTank.ts` — add the shared back-to-index button.
- `src/scenes/gym/*.test.ts`, `src/core/Game.test.ts` — updated/extended tests (rename fallout + discovery/navigation coverage).
- `README.md`, `docs/Game Design Document.md` — dev-run instructions, new-gym-scene convention, layout notes.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — index UI styling constants if shared (e.g. index colours/spacing).

## Related work

- **Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement (AH-0MT97BW7M0056S8S)** — the player gym scene being moved/renamed here.
- **Create Enemy Gym Scene work items (AH-0MT987VA3005YBNK)** — parent epic for the enemy gym scenes listed by this index.
- **Create E1 Scout gym scene (AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q)**, **Create E2 Diver gym scene (AH-0MT99G6310070UXM)**, and **Create E3 Tank gym scene (AH-0MT99I2OC0014MNZ)** — completed enemy scenes that receive the back-to-index button. The original description's dependency ("dependent upon the completion of the first enemy scene") is **satisfied** — E1 Scout is completed.
- **Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes (AH-0MT985FOA008JWM9)** — related; may touch the same shared-helper area; keep the back-button helper in a neutral `src/utils/` location.
- **Bootstrap Phaser + TypeScript project scaffold (AH-0MT97OA3E001DOYW)** — provides Vite, TypeScript, Vitest (dependency of all scenes).
- **Game Design Document for AI_Hell (AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5)** — authoritative spec; §6.4 layout notes updated.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption — rename target:** "rename for consistency" means `GymPlayer.ts` / class+key `GymPlayer` (matching `GymScout`/`GymTank`); display label "Player". If a different name is preferred it is a mechanical rename.
- **Assumption — index location outside the glob folder** (e.g. `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts`): avoids a hard-coded self-exclusion rule; everything in `src/scenes/gym/` is a listable gym scene.
- **Assumption — dev-mode equivalence:** `npm run dev` and `npm run preview` both run the same built bundle/config, so the index is the entry in both; "dev mode" is not a separate runtime flag at this stage.
- **Risk — `import.meta.glob` is build-time:** newly added files are picked up when the glob module is resolved (dev-server restart/HMR or rebuild); not a runtime directory scan. Acceptable for a dev tool — document the expectation.
- **Risk — rename fallout:** moving/renaming the player scene touches `gameConfig.ts`, tests, and GDD references; `tsc --noEmit` and the full Vitest suite are the safety net.
- **Risk — cross-cutting back button:** adding the button to existing scenes touches files owned by other work items (E1/E3 scenes); keep the change minimal (single shared helper + one button per scene) and coordinate with the Refactor Enemy Gym Scenes item.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no game menu, no pause, no per-scene config UI, no URL deep-linking, no search/filter, no thumbnails, no auto-demo mode. Anything beyond a list + immediate switching + back button is out of scope; record extras as linked work items.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the index list the player gym scene separately or only scenes in `src/scenes/gym/`? How are labels/navigation handled?" — Answer (user): "The scene should not hard code the available scenes; they should be discovered by reading the source directory for gym scenes; present them sorted alphabetically." Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q2: "How should 'dev mode' be enabled — URL param, config flag, or always?" — Answer (user): "The server is started with `npm run dev` or `npm run preview` as opposed to a build." Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q3: "When an entry is selected, should it switch immediately or show confirmation?" — Answer (user): "Immediately switch." Source: interactive reply (round 1).
- Q4: "Should the player gym scene (`src/scenes/Gym.ts`) also be listed, and how are labels derived?" — Answer (user): "Move it into `src/scenes/gym/` and rename it for consistency. Labels: raw class filename, but strip `Gym` from the start. Scene key: class name is fine." Source: interactive reply (round 2).
- Q5: "How should users return to the index from a gym scene?" — Answer (user): "Index button" (a small "← INDEX" button in each gym scene). Source: interactive reply (round 3).
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5** – Game Design Document for AI_Hell (completed)
- **AH-0MT7V5UH90023XWR** – Clarify enemy health / one-hit destruction model in GDD (completed)
- **AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V** – Add a Magnet power up (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: completion, create, dependent, dev, enemy, entry, first, game, gym, index, item, mode, page, run, scene, scenes, should, when, work
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: create, dev, enemy, entry, first, game, item, mode, run, scene, scenes, should, when, work
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: completion, create, dependent, item, run, should, when, work

# Create Enemy Gym Scene work items

## Goal (user story)

As a producer, I want a set of well-defined, independently tracked work items for each enemy gym scene (E1–E5 + Boss), so that each scene is planned, implemented, tested, and reviewed as an isolated unit of work.

> **Scope clarification (2026-08-26):** This epic covers ONLY the creation and clarification of the individual work items listed below — it does NOT cover implementing the gym scenes themselves. The six related items are deliberately tracked as **top-level work items, not children of this epic**, so they can be independently planned, prioritised, scheduled, and reviewed. This epic is complete once all six work items exist and are clearly defined; progress on scene code is tracked by those work items, not by this epic.

## Related top-level work items

| Enemy | Work Item | Priority | Key Behaviour |
|-------|-----------|----------|---------------|
| E1 — Scout | **Create E1 Scout gym scene (AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q)** | high | V-formation/line movement, aimed shots (L4+) |
| E2 — Diver | **Create E2 Diver gym scene (AH-0MT99G6310070UXM)** | high | Curved dive trajectory, spread shots (L4+) |
| E3 — Tank | **Create E3 Tank gym scene (AH-0MT99I2OC0014MNZ)** | high | Slow formation, radial burst (L4+) |
| E4 — Phaser | **Create E4 Phaser gym scene (AH-0MT99K3FE008CT13)** | medium | Orbital paths, predictable radial patterns (L5) |
| E5 — Swarm | **Create E5 Swarm gym scene (AH-0MT99N53O0077KHC)** | medium | Fast clusters, sudden direction changes, coordinated bursts (L4) |
| Boss — Central AI | **Create Boss (Central AI) gym scene (AH-0MT99QBDW001O7PE)** | medium | 4-phase health bar, complex bullet patterns |

## Scope per scene (documented in each work item)

- Phaser scene in `src/scenes/gym/` (standalone gym scenes, not shipped with the game) with only that enemy type
- No player ship, no other enemies, no HUD, no power-ups
- Visual representation per GDD §4.1 (§7.1 neon aesthetic)
- Movement/formation pattern per GDD §4.1–4.2
- Explosion animation when enemy is destroyed
- Toggle button for enemy-firing behaviour (off = formation only, on = shooting)
- Audio per GDD §7.3 requirements
- Enemy pass-through verified (per GDD §2.6)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A work item exists for each enemy type E1–E5 and the Boss, each with a clear goal and testable acceptance criteria (verified via `wl show <id>`).
- [ ] Each work item records its priority and key behaviour, and references the GDD (Game Design Document, AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5).

- [ ] Each work item's scope follows the "Scope per scene" section above (enemy only, no player ship/HUD/power-ups, shooting toggle, explosion, audio).

- **Assumption — no external art assets:** All enemy sprites can be drawn programmatically (neon shapes) or via simple placeholders.

# Create E1 Scout gym scene

## Problem statement

Create a Phaser gym scene demonstrating the E1 Scout enemy — the basic formation enemy from GDD §4.1. The scene should show its V-formation/line movement pattern, neon angular appearance, and (at level 4+) its aimed-shooting behaviour. This is the simplest enemy type and should be implemented first to establish the enemy gym pattern.

## Users

- **Player / developer** testing enemy behaviour — wants to see the Scout's formation flight and shooting patterns in isolation.
- **AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — need a reference enemy implementation that can be replicated for E2–E5 with different behaviours.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want to see the Scout fly in a V-formation across the screen so I can verify the formation movement code works correctly.
- As a **developer**, I want to click a button to destroy a random Scout and see its explosion animation so I can verify destruction logic.
- As a **developer**, I want to toggle the Scout's shooting behaviour on/off so I can test both formation-only and shooting modes independently.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Gym scene exists:** A Phaser scene (`src/scenes/gym/GymScout.ts`) renders Scout enemies in a V-formation moving across the screen.
- [ ] **AC2 — Scout visual style:** Scouts render as small, angular neon shapes (green `#00ff00` per GDD §4.1) consistent with the player ship aesthetic.
- [ ] **AC3 — V-formation movement:** Enemies move as a group in a V-formation pattern, advancing across the screen. Formation maintains shape during movement.
- [ ] **AC4 — Explode button:** A button on-screen destroys a random Scout enemy with an explosion animation when clicked.
- [ ] **AC5 — Toggle shoot button:** A button toggles whether Scouts fire aimed shots (simulating Level 4+ behaviour). When off, Scouts only fly formation. When on, they periodically fire aimed projectiles at the player position.
- [ ] **AC6 — Enemy pass-through verified:** Scouts pass freely through each other without collision (per GDD §2.6).
- [ ] **AC7 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] **AC8 — Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Engine:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript.

- **Firing:** When shoot mode is toggled on, Scouts fire aimed shots at the current player position (simulating a player ship that may not be on screen — use a default or last-known position).
- **Audio:** Play distinct sound effects for spawn, movement hum (optional), and destruction. Per GDD §7.3 enemy audio requirements.

## Problem statement

Create a Phaser gym scene demonstrating the E4 Phaser enemy — the orbital pattern attacker from GDD §4.1. The scene should show its circular neon ring appearance with a central core, slow orbital path movement, and predictable repeating firing cycles. This is a Level 5 exclusive enemy with high pattern-based challenge.

## Users

- **Player / developer** testing enemy behaviour — wants to see the Phaser's orbital movement and predictable firing patterns in isolation.
- **AI agents implementing AI_Hell** — need a reference implementation of orbital movement and pattern-based firing logic.

### Example user stories

- As a **developer**, I want to see Phaser enemies move in fixed orbital paths around a central point so I can verify the orbital movement code works correctly.
- As a **developer**, I want to click a button to destroy a random Phaser and see its explosion animation so I can verify destruction logic.
- As a **developer**, I want to toggle the Phaser's shooting behaviour on/off so I can test both orbital-only and shooting modes independently.
- As a **developer**, I want to see clear tell animations and advance audio cues (≥ 500 ms lead time) before the Phaser fires so I can verify the telegraphing system.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Gym scene exists:** A Phaser scene (`src/scenes/gym/GymPhaser.ts`) renders Phaser enemies in orbital paths around a central point.
- [ ] **AC2 — Phaser visual style:** Phasers render as circular neon rings with a central core (magenta `#ff00ff` per GDD §4.1) consistent with the player ship aesthetic.
- [ ] **AC3 — Orbital movement:** Enemies move slowly in fixed orbital paths around a central point on screen.
- [ ] **AC4 — Predictable firing patterns:** When shoot mode is toggled on, Phasers fire in predictable, repeating cycles (radial or aimed patterns) with clear tell animations and advance audio cues (≥ 500 ms lead time) before each firing cycle.
- [ ] **AC5 — Explode button:** A button on-screen destroys a random Phaser enemy with an explosion animation when clicked.
- [ ] **AC6 — Toggle shoot button:** A button toggles whether Phasers fire. When off, Phasers only orbit. When on, they fire in predictable repeating cycles.
- [ ] **AC7 — Enemy pass-through verified:** Phasers pass freely through each other without collision (per GDD §2.6).
- [ ] **AC8 — All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

- **Engine:** Phaser v4 + TypeScript.
- **Gym scope:** This scene is a standalone gym scene (not shipped with the game) — no player ship, no other enemy types, no HUD, no power-ups.

# Ship configuration file: load and save values

## Problem statement

Ship tuning values (thrust acceleration, max speed, ship size, thrust flame length, colours) are currently hard-coded as constants in src/core/constants.ts (GDD §2.2 Newtonian-drift model). There is no way to persist tuned values to a file, which blocks the gym-scene slider work item that needs to write slider values back to a config file.

## User stories

- As a developer/tuner, I want ship values to live in a config file that the game reads at startup, so I can tweak values without editing code.
- As a developer/tuner, I want to write the current values back to that config file, so a save action in the gym scene persists my tuning session.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Config file source of truth:** Ship configuration values (at minimum: thrust acceleration, max speed, ship size, thrust flame length) are loaded from a config file at game startup when the file exists.
- [ ] **AC2 — Fallback defaults:** When no config file exists, the game uses the existing built-in constants from src/core/constants.ts (no crash, no missing values).
- [ ] **AC3 — Save mechanism:** A saveShipConfig(values) API writes the supplied values to the config file (location/format decided; JSON expected).
- [ ] **AC4 — Round-trip:** Loading a config file that was previously saved reproduces the saved values exactly.
- [ ] **AC5 — Integration point:** The config module exposes a typed interface matching the ship config fields so the gym scene's slider work item can read and write through it.
- [ ] **AC6 — Tests:** Unit tests cover load-when-present, load-when-absent (fallback), and save round-trip.

## Design questions (resolve during intake/plan)

- This is a browser game (Phaser, web-first per GDD §6.3). Where does the config file live?
  - Option A: a JSON file in public/ fetched at startup (read-only to browser; save triggers a local JSON download).
  - Option B: localStorage-backed persistence (read/write without server).
  - Operator decision needed; recommendation: Option B for the save button to truly persist, Option A for values in an editable file. May combine (A for defaults shipped, B for user overrides).

## Key Files

- src/core/constants.ts — source of the current hard-coded values that must become configurable.
- src/utils/movement.ts — consumes thrust/maxSpeed via MovementConfig.
- src/entities/Player.ts — consumes the constants (SHIP_SIZE, colours, THRUST_ACCELERATION, MAX_SPEED).

## Dependency

This item is a prerequisite for the gym sliders + save-button work item (parent task depends on this).

# Gym scene: ship config sliders, save button, half-speed ship

## Problem statement

The gym scene (src/scenes/Gym.ts) renders the player ship with hard-coded tuning constants (src/core/constants.ts). There is no in-game way to adjust the ship's configuration values, and no way to persist adjustments. This work item adds sliders to the gym scene for each ship configuration value, a save button that writes the current values to the config file (mechanism provided by dependency AH-0MT9FRVF00086TO3), and halves the ship's speed.

## User stories

- As a player/developer, I want sliders in the gym scene for each ship configuration value (thrust acceleration, max speed, ship size, thrust flame length, and colour values where feasible) so I can tune and preview the ship's feel live.
- As a player/developer, I want a Save button that persists the current slider values to the config file, so my tuning survives restarts.
- As a player/developer, I want the ship half as fast as the current default, so the fuel/thrust feel is adjusted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Slider per config value:** The gym scene shows a slider for each numeric ship configuration value (at minimum: thrust acceleration, max speed, ship size, thrust flame length; colour values as a stretch/secondary set). Moving a slider updates the live ship behaviour immediately (rerendering the ship and its physics).
- [ ] **AC2 — Live update:** Changing max-speed/thrust sliders changes the actual movement physics applied to the ship in the gym scene without restart; changing ship size / flame length re-renders the ship.
- [ ] **AC3 — Save button:** A Save button writes the current slider values to the config file via the config module from AH-0MT9FRVF00086TO3 (dependent work item). A confirmation/status message indicates success/failure.
- [ ] **AC4 — Initial values loaded:** When the game starts, sliders are initialised from the config file (if present) or the built-in constants (fallback).
- [ ] **AC5 — Half speed:** The ship's default speed is halved: MAX_SPEED 350 → 175 px/s (and THRUST_ACCELERATION 600 → 300 px/s² so the half-speed feel is consistent).
- [ ] **AC6 — Tests:** Existing test suite passes; new unit tests cover slider→config value mapping and the half-speed constants.

## Assumptions to confirm with operator

- What exactly does half speed mean: halve MAX_SPEED only (350→175), or also THRUST_ACCELERATION (600→300)? Recommendation: both, for a consistent feel.
- Colour values: sliders are awkward for colours — recommend HTML colour inputs or exclude from the slider set (keep them save-able but not slider-controlled). Awaiting operator preference.
- Save mechanism shape depends on the design decision in dependency AH-0MT9FRVF00086TO3 (localStorage vs JSON file download vs public/ JSON).

## Key Files

- src/scenes/Gym.ts — the scene to enhance with sliders + save button.
- src/entities/Player.ts — consumes the config; must accept runtime-updated config values.
- src/core/constants.ts — values to be halved and made slider-adjustable.
- src/utils/movement.ts — MovementConfig consumption.

Blocked by AH-0MT9FRVF00086TO3 (Ship configuration file: load and save values) — the save button writes through its API.

# Thrust flame invisible on player ship; should scale with thrustAcceleration

## Problem statement

The player ship's thrust flame is drawn as a static, always-full-size triangle whenever a direction key is held — it never scales with the ship's `thrustAcceleration`. The result is that the flame is barely perceptible (default `shipSize=20`, `thrustFlameLength=0.75` → only 15px of fixed flame) and gives no visual indication of thrust magnitude.

## Desired change

The flame must **animate**: when thrusting it grows from length **0** to its maximum length, and the growth rate is proportional to `thrustAcceleration`:

- **Max flame length** = `shipSize × thrustFlameLength` (unchanged semantics — at `thrustFlameLength=1` the flame is roughly the size of the ship).
- **Growth rate** ∝ `thrustAcceleration`: higher thrust → flame reaches full length faster; at thrust `0` the flame never grows (stays at 0 → invisible, consistent with "starts at 0").
- **Shrink rate** = **4× the growth rate**: when thrust stops (key released) the flame shrinks back to 0, decaying 4× faster than it grew. Growth resumes from the current length if thrust is re-applied before fully decayed; length never goes below 0.
- Growth/shrink must be **delta-time (`dt`) based**, so the animation is framerate-independent; driven each frame from `Player.update()` (where thrust input is already polled).
- Length grows toward the *current* (config-live) max so `setConfig` re-tuning (gym sliders) takes effect mid-animation.

## Users

- **Player**: pressing a direction key shows a visible flame that builds up; the stronger the ship's thrust, the quicker the flame springs to full size. Releasing the key makes the flame die back quickly (4× faster than it grew).

User stories:

- *As a player, when I hold a direction key on a ship with high thrustAcceleration, I see a flame that quickly grows to full size (≈ ship length at thrustFlameLength=1), so I can feel the power of my thrust.*
- *As a player, when I release the key, the flame rapidly shrinks back to nothing, so I get clear feedback that thrust has stopped.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Flame animates from 0:** When thrust input is applied, the flame length starts at 0 and increases over time toward `shipSize × thrustFlameLength` (at `thrustFlameLength=1` the max flame length ≈ ship size). Tests verify length starts at 0 and grows monotonically while thrust is held (dt-based, framerate-independent).
- [ ] **AC2 — Growth rate proportional to thrustAcceleration:** A higher `thrustAcceleration` reaches full flame length in less time than a lower one; at `thrustAcceleration=0` the flame length stays 0 while thrusting. Verified by unit tests comparing elapsed time-to-full (or lengths after equal dt) across configs.
- [ ] **AC3 — Flame shrinks at 4× growth rate:** Releasing thrust causes the flame length to decay to 0 at 4× the speed it grew; re-applying thrust before full decay resumes growth from the current length; length never clamps below 0.
- [ ] **AC4 — Config-live and framerate-independent:** Growth/shrink is computed per-frame from `dt` (not per-frame fixed increments) and targets the current config's `shipSize × thrustFlameLength` (gym slider / `setConfig` changes take effect immediately, including mid-growth).
- [ ] **AC5 — Rendering & tests:** The flame is visibly drawn throughout growth (not toggle-drawn only at full length); existing Player/movement tests pass; new Player tests cover the animation without needing pixel-level assertions (exposing length as observable state or via a testable pure helper).
- [ ] **AC6 — Docs & suite:** All related documentation updated (code comments in `Player.ts`, README/GDD references if any); full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Config semantics unchanged: `thrustFlameLength` remains a multiplier of `shipSize` (max length), `shipSize` unchanged. Existing `thrustAcceleration` range (gym slider 0–1200, default 300).
- Flame still drawn opposite the thrust direction (behind the ship) with the existing outer/inner color scheme.
- Keep the existing on/off input semantics: thrusting = any direction key held; a length which starts at 0 makes the flame invisible when thrustAcceleration is 0.
- No external art assets; all flame rendering stays procedural in `Player._drawFlame()`.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Player.ts` — draws flame at fixed length `flameLen = shipSize × flameLength` whenever `_flameVisible`; `update()` only toggles `_flameVisible` on change; no animation state.
- `src/core/config.ts` — `thrustFlameLength` (default 0.75), `thrustAcceleration` (default 300), `shipSize` (default 20).
- `src/scenes/Gym.ts` — sliders: `thrustAcceleration` 0–1200, `thrustFlameLength` 0.1–2, `shipSize` 4–60.
- `src/utils/movement.ts` — pure physics model (no rendering); untouched by this change.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Player.ts` — add flame length animation state (current length, growth/shrink per-frame using `dt`), drive it from `update()`, scale `_drawFlame()` by the current length.
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — unit tests for AC1–AC4 (animation via exposed state or pure helper).
- `src/core/config.ts` / `src/core/constants.ts` — read-only references (values already wired in).
- `README.md` / `docs/Game Design Document.md` — only if flame/animation behavior is described there (verify during implementation).

## Related work

- AH-0MT9WZCJC000ZA1M — "Integrate config module with constants, Player, and tests" (open, plan_complete): Player consuming runtime config incl. flame rendering — this bug builds on that wiring.
- AH-0MT9FRVF00086TO3 — "Ship configuration file: load and save values" (completed).
- AH-0MT9FS3DL0084Z6V — "Gym scene: ship config sliders, save button, half-speed ship" (completed) — slider ranges for thrust/flame.
- AH-0MTA8DMBH007MEHG — "Gym scene sliders bound to live ship config" (open) — `setConfig` live re-render path.
- AH-0MT97BW7M0056S8S — "Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement" (completed) — original flame "small flame" placeholder requirement (GDD §2.2).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk (verify at implementation):** the report says the flame is "invisible". `add.existing` puts the Player on both display and update lists, so `update()` runs and the flame *should* render; likely the 15px static flame is simply too subtle. Implementation must confirm rendering works at small lengths (a genuine render bug, if present, is in scope for this bug).
- **Assumption:** "start at 0" applies per thrust press; a held key grows the flame monotonically and it stays at max while held (no flicker/oscillation) until release.
- **Assumption:** growth resumes mid-flight when a key is re-pressed before the decay completes (length clamps to `[0, maxLength]`).
- **Assumption:** proportional means *linear* rate ∝ thrustAcceleration; exact scaling constant (time-to-full at default 300) is a tuning choice to be made at implementation — flag for Producer if a specific feel target exists (e.g., "full length in ~0.5s at 300 thrust").
- **Risk (scope creep):** pulse/flicker animation, per-direction flame physics, or flame colors driven by thrust are out of scope — record as separate work items if desired.
- **Assumption:** `thrustFlameLength=0` (slider min 0.1 so not reachable via UI) would yield max length 0 → flame never visible; acceptable edge case.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Growth dynamics — purely proportional to the thrustAcceleration config value (instantaneous), or animate/ramp up over time while thrusting?" — Answer (user): "I meant grow to maximum length in an amount of time proportional to thrustAcceleration. Where maximum length is the thrustFlameLength. And a thrustFlameLength is roughly the size of the ship." Source: interactive reply (intake session, 2026-08-26). Interpretation: temporal ramp, max = `shipSize × thrustFlameLength`, flame at `thrustFlameLength=1` ≈ ship size. Prior answer: none (first pass). Research: `src/entities/Player.ts` `_drawFlame()` currently static at fixed length; no time-based state exists.
- Q: "Higher thrustAcceleration → flame reach full length faster or slower?" — Answer (user): "faster". Source: interactive reply (intake session, 2026-08-26). Research: growth rate ∝ thrustAcceleration; at 0 thrust the flame stays 0.
- Q: "Release behavior — shrink back toward 0 (on similar time scale) or vanish instantly?" — Answer (user): "shrink at 4x the speed it grew". Source: interactive reply (intake session, 2026-08-26). Research: symmetric decay state, 4× growth rate, resumes growth from current length on re-apply.

# Direction-neutral ship shape: circle with engines at top, bottom, and each side

## Problem statement

The player ship currently renders as a cyan chevron pointing "up" (`src/entities/Player.ts`), a silhouette that communicates a direction of travel. In a thrust-based, 360°-movement game the player has no fixed heading, so the hull should be direction-neutral and the thrust direction must instead be readable from the engines' flames.

## Users

- **Players** — need a ship silhouette that never implies a heading, with thrust read off the engine flames.
- **AI agents / developers** — need a deterministic mapping from input → firing engines so behaviour is testable and keeps working with the config-driven tuning (gym sliders, `setConfig`).

### Example user stories

- As a **player**, I want the ship body to look the same no matter which way I'm about to thrust, so I can't be misled about a fixed forward direction.
- As a **player**, I want the flame(s) to visibly come from the engine(s) on the side(s) opposite my thrust, so my movement intent is readable from the ship itself.
- As a **developer**, I want a pure, tested function mapping thrust input to firing engines so the flame logic is verifiable without pixel assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Direction-neutral body:** The player ship body is replaced with a silhouette invariant under 90° rotation (no nose/heading cue). The chosen shape must follow GDD §7.2's geometric palette (geometric, angular shapes — triangles, chevrons, hexagons, rings; no organic forms). "Circle" remains a proposal; a ring/hexagon is the GDD-aligned default. Operator confirmed scope: **player ship only** — enemy shapes are not changed.
- [ ] **AC2 — Four engine ports:** The hull has four small engine ports at top, bottom, left, and right; flames only ever originate from port(s), never from the hull centre.
- [ ] **AC3 — Engine firing rule:** Cardinal thrust fires exactly the engine whose outward normal opposes the thrust (thrust right → left engine). Diagonal thrust fires the two engines whose normals oppose the thrust components, each flame scaled by its component (e.g., up+right → bottom and left engines). No thrust input → no flames.
- [ ] **AC4 — Config wiring preserved:** Rendering remains driven by `ShipConfig` (`shipColor`, `shipSize`, `thrustFlameColor`, `thrustFlameInnerColor`, `thrustFlameLength`) and continues to work with live `setConfig` and the gym scene sliders.
- [ ] **AC5 — Tests:** A pure helper mapping MovementInput → firing engines/directions is covered for no-thrust, all four cardinal, and diagonal cases; flame length scaling per component is covered. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
- [ ] **AC6 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (GDD §7.2 / player ship description notes the direction-neutral hull and engine-flame rule; code comments updated in `Player.ts`).

## Constraints

- Follow GDD §7.2 visual style: geometric/angular silhouettes, neon glow/outline, palette `#00ffff` player colour — no new art assets (Phaser `Graphics` rendering only).
- Coordinate with in-progress AH-0MTAF5YLT009TXAM (thrust flame invisible; flame length ∝ thrustAcceleration) — same flame-rendering code in `Player.ts`; avoid clobbering that work.
- `shipSize` keeps its existing meaning (half-size / body radius used by physics-adjacent callers and the config module).
- No physics changes (`utils/movement.ts` untouched).

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Player.ts` draws a cyan chevron pointing "up" (`_redraw()`), with a single triangle flame drawn from the hull centre opposite the thrust direction (`_drawFlame()`), toggle driven by `update()`.
- Config values come from `core/config.ts` (`ShipConfig`); sliders in the gym scene live-tune via `setConfig`.
- Flame visibility bug (flame length ∝ thrust) is being fixed in AH-0MTAF5YLT009TXAM.

## Desired change

- Replace the chevron body with a direction-neutral shape (GDD-aligned) plus four engine ports at the cardinal points.
- Replace the single centre-anchored flame with per-engine flames: draw a flame from each port whose outward normal opposes the current thrust vector, each scaled by the thrust component along that axis.
- Keep the flame colours/scale knobs config-driven so the existing sliders and `setConfig` keep working.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/entities/Player.ts` — body redraw (`_redraw`) and engine-based flame drawing (`_drawFlame`); engine geometry from `shipSize`.
- `src/entities/Player.test.ts` — updated/new tests for body symmetry and engine-firing logic.
- `src/utils/` (or inline in `Player.ts`) — pure engine-selection helper mapping input → firing engines, for testability.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.2 / player ship description updated for direction-neutral hull.

## Related work

- AH-0MTAF5YLT009TXAM — *Thrust flame invisible on player ship; should scale with thrustAcceleration* (critical, in-progress): overlaps in `_drawFlame`; flame length ∝ thrust semantics apply to the per-engine flames here.
- AH-0MTA8DMBH007MEHG — *Gym scene sliders bound to live ship config* (open, high): depends on `setConfig` continuing to work after redraw.
- AH-0MT9WZ0AC0002X58 — *Define ShipConfig type, defaults, load, and save functions* (open, medium): source of tuning values used by the renderer.
- AH-0MT97BW7M0056S8S — *Create gym scene with player ship and thrust-based space movement* (completed): original scene/player work.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Rendering is hard to assert in tests** (happy-dom / Phaser Graphics): mitigate by extracting a pure input → engines mapping and testing it directly; keep body-shape verification to structural assertions (e.g., drawing command count / geometry) or documented manual check.
- **Overlap with the in-progress critical flame item**: coordinate sequencing; if both touch `_drawFlame` the merge must be careful — make the flame-scaling item a prerequisite dependency.
- **GDD "no organic forms"**: a plain filled disc is borderline; prefer ring/hexagon or explicitly amend GDD if the operator prefers a circle (scope decision deferred).
- **Assumption**: enemy ship shapes are out of scope (operator confirmed, player only).
- **Scope-creep guard**: engine glow/particle effects, enemy reshapes, new config keys, or animation are NOT in scope — record as new work items if desired, not in this item.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q** – Create E1 Scout gym scene (completed)
- **AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5** – Game Design Document for AI_Hell (completed)
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ** – Gym index scene (in-progress)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: bottom, circle, direction, engines, flame, high, intent, needs, shape, ship, side, small, thrust, top, travel
- `README.md` — matched: bottom, direction, high, intent, needs, priority, ship, side, small, source, thrust, top
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: high, priority, ship, small, source

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Engine firing:** "When thrusting, should the flame come from (a) the single engine opposite thrust (thrust right → left engine fires, morphing to one/two engines for diagonals) or (b) all engines whose outward normal opposes the thrust vector (diagonal thrust → the two adjacent engines both fire with scaled flames)?" — **Answer (user):** "b" — all engines whose outward normal opposes the thrust vector fire; diagonal thrust → the two adjacent engines both fire with scaled (per-component) flames. Source: interactive reply, `/intake` session 2026-08-26.
- **Q2 — Silhouette:** "Is a circle confirmed for the body, or should I keep it as a proposal vs. other direction-neutral geometric options (e.g., ring/hexagon — closer to GDD §7.2 angular palette where 'no organic forms' is stated)?" — **Answer (user):** "proposal — follow GDD" — the circle remains a proposal; the final shape must follow GDD §7.2's geometric palette (geometric, angular shapes; no organic forms), which favours ring/hexagon over a plain filled disc unless the GDD is amended. Source: interactive reply, `/intake` session 2026-08-26.
- **Q3 — Scope:** "Direction-neutrality for the player ship only — or should enemy shapes (Scout/Diver chevrons) be reconsidered too, since they also imply a heading?" — **Answer (user):** "player only" — enemy ship shapes are out of scope. Source: interactive reply, `/intake` session 2026-08-26.

# Intake Brief — Ship deceleration when no inputs, with slider (AH-0MTAFH1ZF003EGDF)

## Headline

Add linear deceleration (friction) to the ship movement model so it slows to a stop when no directional inputs are held, tunable via a new slider in the Gym scene panel (default 100 px/s², range 0–400 px/s²), and update the GDD §2.2 to reflect the new behaviour.

## Problem Statement

The ship currently uses pure Newtonian zero-friction drift (GDD §2.2): releasing all keys preserves velocity forever, so the ship coasts indefinitely. In a bullet-hell game this makes precise positioning harder — the ship should instead slow to a stop when no inputs are held. The deceleration rate must be player-tunable so the feel can be adjusted.

## Users

- **Player** — wants responsive, controllable movement; the ship should come to rest when they stop pressing keys, not drift indefinitely.
- **Developer/tuner** — adjusts ship feel via the Gym scene tuning panel; needs a slider for the deceleration rate, persisted like the other ship config values.

### User stories

- As a player, I want the ship to slow to a stop when I release all direction keys, so I can hold a position and aim precisely.
- As a developer, I want a slider in the Gym panel to control how quickly the ship decelerates, so I can tune the feel without editing code.
- As a developer, I want the deceleration value persisted with the rest of the ship config, so my tuning survives page reloads.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Movement model:** When no direction keys are held, the ship's velocity decays linearly toward zero at the configured deceleration rate (px/s²); velocity reaches exactly zero and stops (no oscillation / no residual drift). With deceleration = 0, the previous zero-friction drift behaviour is preserved.
- **AC2 — Config plumbing:** A new `frictionDeceleration` (or equivalent) field is added to `ShipConfig` (default 100), re-exported from `constants.ts`, loaded/saved via `loadShipConfig`/`saveShipConfig`, and passed into the movement model via `MovementConfig`.
- **AC3 — Gym slider:** The Gym scene panel gains one slider for the deceleration value, with range 0–400 px/s² (min 0), a live value label, and live application to the ship — consistent with the existing ship-tuning sliders. Saved via the existing Save button.
- **AC4 — Tests:** Unit tests cover: velocity decays to (near) zero with no input; decay rate scales with the deceleration value; deceleration = 0 preserves pure drift; thrusting is unaffected by deceleration (deceleration applies only when no input is held). Existing tests asserting "zero friction drift" are updated to the new default.
- **AC5 — Docs:** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.2 is updated to replace the "zero friction, no deceleration" wording with a description of the tunable deceleration behaviour, and the ship tuning panel documentation is kept consistent.
- **AC6 — Validation:** Full project test suite passes with the changes; all related documentation is updated (code comments, README where relevant).

## Constraints

- Must not change thrust behaviour — deceleration applies only when no direction key is held.
- Movement model stays pure/side-effect-free in `src/utils/movement.ts`.
- `MovementConfig` currently has only `thrust`/`maxSpeed`; deceleration must be threaded through Player (`setConfig`) and the config module.
- Persist via the existing `localStorage` config mechanism (`CONFIG_STORAGE_KEY`, `ai-hell-ship-config`).

## Existing State

- `src/utils/movement.ts` — `applyThrust` returns velocity unchanged when no input ("zero friction / drift" comment); `MovementConfig` = `{thrust, maxSpeed}`.
- `src/core/config.ts` — `ShipConfig` has `thrustAcceleration`, `maxSpeed`, `shipSize`, `thrustFlameLength`, and colour fields; no friction field.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — re-exports `DEFAULT_CONFIG` values.
- `src/scenes/Gym.ts` — `SLIDER_RANGES` drives one slider per numeric config value, plus color inputs and Save; `_readPanelValues`/`_applyPanelValues`/`_onControlInput` apply live.
- `src/utils/movement.test.ts` — tests assert "preserves velocity when no thrust (zero friction drift)" and "drifts without input (zero friction)".
- GDD §2.2 — explicitly documents zero-friction drift.

## Desired Change

1. Add `frictionDeceleration: number` to `ShipConfig` (default 100), `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, and re-export in `constants.ts`; add a `friction` (or similar) field to `MovementConfig`.
2. In `applyThrust` (movement model), when no input is held, reduce velocity magnitude linearly by `friction × dt`, clamped at zero; keep it a pure function.
3. Thread the value through `Player` constructor/`setConfig` → `MovementConfig`.
4. Add the slider to the Gym panel (`SLIDER_RANGES` entry: min 0, max 400, step e.g. 5), with live apply and labels; persistence handled by the existing Save flow.
5. Update `movement.test.ts` (zero-friction assertions → deceleration assertions) and add new tests; update GDD §2.2.

## Key Files

- `src/utils/movement.ts` — Add deceleration to `applyThrust` (no-input branch); extend `MovementConfig`.
- `src/core/config.ts` — Add `frictionDeceleration` to `ShipConfig` + `DEFAULT_CONFIG`.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — Re-export the new default.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — Thread deceleration from `ShipConfig` into `MovementConfig` (constructor + `setConfig`).
- `src/scenes/Gym.ts` — Add slider entry to `SLIDER_RANGES`.
- `src/utils/movement.test.ts` — Update/add unit tests.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Update §2.2.

## Related Work

- Gym scene: ship config sliders, save button, half-speed ship (AH-0MT9FS3DL0084Z6V) — completed; established the panel slider pattern.
- Ship configuration file: load and save values (AH-0MT9FRVF00086TO3) — completed; config persistence mechanism.
- Gym scene sliders bound to live ship config (AH-0MTA8DMBH007MEHG) — open; live binding pattern.
- Define ShipConfig type, defaults, load, and save functions (AH-0MT9WZ0AC0002X58) — open.
- Halve the default ship speed (AH-0MTA7IMXL000NXON) — completed; precedent for ship-feel tuning changes.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption:** Deceleration applies **only when no input is held** (per request wording); while thrusting, behaviour is unchanged.
- **Assumption:** Units are px/s² (linear friction), consistent with `thrustAcceleration`.
- **Assumption:** Slider lives in the Gym scene panel (confirmed Q2); a settings menu is out of scope.
- **Risk (scope creep):** Power-up interactions (e.g., P5 Speed Boost) with deceleration are out of scope — handled by a separate future work item if needed.
- **Risk (edge case):** Ensure velocity clamps at zero (no overshoot / negative velocity) when friction would reduce speed past zero — the movement function must use `Math.max(0, ...)` or equivalent.
- **Scope-creep risk:** This intake captures the deceleration feature. Tuning the exact default value, range, or step through playtesting is a separate refinement; the defaults (100 px/s², 0–400 range) are sufficient to start.
- **Design note:** Default 100 px/s² gives stop-from-max-speed (~175 px/s) in ~1.75 s; slider min 0 re-enables the old zero-friction drift for experimentation.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1: "Deceleration semantics & default — linear friction in px/s² (same units as thrustAcceleration)? Proposed default ~100 px/s², slider range 0–400 px/s², min 0 preserving zero-friction drift. Good, or different default/range / proportional damping?" — Answer (operator@session): "Suggestion is good". Final: linear friction in px/s², default 100, range 0–400, min 0. Root cause: src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts -> loadGymSceneModules() globs ../scenes/gym/*.ts with eager:true. The pattern matches the gym .test.ts modules, bundling Vitest's runtime into the browser bundle and executing it client-side; the runtime isTestModulePath filter only removes tests from the index list, not from the bundle. discovered-from:AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ

Desired change: exclude *.test.ts at the glob-pattern level (Vite supports negative patterns, e.g. ['../scenes/gym/*.ts','!../scenes/gym/*.test.ts']) so test files never enter the browser bundle; keep the runtime filter as a defensive second layer. Verify npm run dev renders the gym index with zero console errors, npm run build passes, and the full Vitest suite stays green.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] AC1: loadGymSceneModules excludes .test.ts from the glob pattern itself (no test module in the eager bundle).
- [ ] AC2: npm run dev renders the gym index in-browser with no unhandled errors from Vitest/test modules.

data.description: Discovered while fixing AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q (E1 Scout gym: invisible enemies). Same class of bug affects the E2 Diver and E3 Tank gyms: entity _drawBody() calls lineStyle() BEFORE graphics.clear(); Phaser Graphics is command-buffered and clear() wipes styles queued before it (re-applying only the default white 1px stroke). Effect verified in a real browser (headless happy-dom tests cannot see pixels): Tank formation renders TANK_COLOR (0xff6600) at ~25% intensity (sample pixels 62,25,0) instead of full orange; Diver renders grey (43,43,43) instead of DIVER_COLOR (0xffff00). Fix (per entity, in src/entities/Tank.ts and src/entities/Diver.ts): move lineStyle() call inside _drawBody() AFTER clear() — same one-function reorder as the Scout fix committed for AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q. Verify in browser after fix; consider a command-buffer regression test like Scout.test.ts. discovered-from:AH-0MT994ESD000RP1Q

# Extract reusable gym formation-scene core library

## Problem statement

`GymScout.ts`, `GymDiver.ts`, and `GymTank.ts` are ~90% identical: formation spawn loop, EXPLODE/SHOOT HUD buttons, status line, hint line, back-to-index button, formation drift + respawn, per-entity `applyFormationPosition` update, bullet collection/advance/off-screen removal, `_bulletOffScreen`, `_respawnX`, and the `labelStyle`/`_addButton` helpers. Only the entity class, formation-offset builder, tuning constants, fire method (`tryFireAimedBullet` / `tryFireSpreadBurst` / `tryFireRadialBurst`), status label, and hint text differ.

## Goal (user story)

As a **developer**, I want a single, tested core library — a generic gym formation-scene base class parameterised by entity-specific config plus shared formation-offset builders — so each enemy gym scene (current and future E4/E5/Boss) is a thin class supplying only its own config.

## Scope

- **In scope:** create `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` (or equivalent path excluded from index discovery) — a `Phaser.Scene` subclass with an `EnemyFormationConfig` describing: entity factory, formation-offset builder, spacing/start/drift constants, status label, hint text, and a per-entity fire-collection callback. Encapsulate: formation spawn (`add.existing` per entity), EXPLODE/SHOOT buttons, status line, hint line, back-to-index button, drift + respawn (`_respawnX`), bullet lifecycle (advance + `_bulletOffScreen`). Also extract the three formation-offset builders (`buildVFormationOffsets`, `buildDiverFormationOffsets`, `buildRectFormationOffsets`) into a shared pure module with their own unit tests.
- **Out of scope:** rewriting the three scenes (separate child items); changing GymIndex/discovery; entity visuals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Base class exists:** `GymFormationScene` (or equivalent) encapsulates the shared boilerplate and is parameterised by a config object with entity factory, offset builder, constants, labels, and fire collection; it is placed so the gym index does **not** list it as an entry.
- [ ] **AC2 — Formation builders extracted:** `buildVFormationOffsets`, `buildDiverFormationOffsets`, `buildRectFormationOffsets` move to a shared module (with the individual `FormationOffset` interfaces consolidated) and their existing geometry semantics (same offsets for the same count) are unchanged.
- [ ] **AC3 — Base class unit-tested:** new tests cover: formation spawn count + display-list membership, EXPLODE destroys one alive entity and no-ops when none remain, SHOOT toggle propagates to entities, drift + respawn, and off-screen bullet removal — using a stub entity type.
- [ ] **AC4 — No regression:** the three existing scene test suites still pass against the current scenes *before* they are rewritten (extraction is behaviour-neutral).

## Suggested implementation

1. Create `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` with `EnemyFormationConfig` and the scene class (ports of the current `create()`/`update()` logic, parameterised).
2. Create `src/utils/formations.ts` (or `src/scenes/gym/core/formations.ts`) consolidating the three `build*FormationOffsets` functions + `FormationOffset` interface.
3. Write tests (TDD) for the base class using a stub entity (tests first, then implementation).
4. Keep the current `GymScout/GymDiver/GymTank` untouched until their own rewrite items run.

# Write ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md best-practice guide

## Problem statement

The enemy gym scenes were built independently, triplicating formation-scene boilerplate. The core library (see parent epic and "Extract reusable gym formation-scene core library") standardises how enemy gym scenes are built, but there is no document recording the design rules and best practices that E4/E5/Boss and future scenes must follow.

## Goal (user story)

As a **developer**, I want a single `ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` guide that explains the enemy design (GDD §4.x) and how to implement enemy gym scenes with the core library, so new scenes follow the standard without maintaining three copies of the boilerplate.

## Scope

- **In scope:** create `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` with: enemy roles/attributes recap (per GDD §4.1/§4.2/§4.3, notably E4 Phaser orbital patterns, E5 Swarm clustering, Boss phases); the core-library architecture (config interface, base class responsibilities); best practice for adding a new enemy gym scene (thin scene = config + entity factory + fire collection; preserve test accessors; where constants live; discovery/exclusion rules); testing guidance (what per-scene tests must assert, using the existing GymScout/GymDiver/GymTank suites as exemplars) and known gotchas (`lineStyle()` after `clear()` for browser rendering, `add.existing` for display-list membership).
- **Out of scope:** implementing any new scene; rewriting existing scenes (separate items); repo `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Guide exists:** `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` is created and accurate against the actual core library API and the three rewritten scenes.
- [ ] **AC2 — New-scene checklist:** the guide includes a step-by-step checklist for creating an enemy gym scene with the core library (config → entity factory → fire collection → accessors → tests → discovery).
- [ ] **AC3 — Best-practice rules:** the guide documents the browser rendering gotchas (`lineStyle()` after `clear()`, `add.existing`) and the test-accessor convention.
- [ ] **AC4 — GDD cross-reference:** the guide maps each enemy (E1–E5, Boss) to its GDD section and key behaviours.

## Suggested implementation

1. Study the core library (from "Extract reusable gym formation-scene core library") and the three rewritten scenes.
2. Write the guide, cross-referencing `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.x.
3. Update the E4/E5/Boss work items to reference the guide (separate child item, if applicable).

data.author: Map
data.comment:
Bug fix pushed to dev, see commit 8ff1019.

Issue reported during playtest: 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading _justDown)' on keydown/keyup. The initial input code used Phaser.Keyboard.JustDown with keys from addKeys(['W','A','S','D']) (array form — not a documented API; keys did not map to W/A/S/D) causing undefined keys at runtime. JustDown is also edge-triggered (fires once per press), which is wrong for continuous thrust.

Fix: poll cursors + WASD isDown state every frame (level-triggered) so a held key applies continuous thrust; use the documented addKeys('W,A,S,D') comma-separated string. Extracted the key->input mapping into a pure util (src/utils/input.ts) with 6 new unit tests (40 total, all passing).

data.author: Map
data.comment: Rejected manual review fixed: invisible Scouts. Root cause — Phaser Graphics is command-buffered; _drawBody() called lineStyle() BEFORE graphics.clear() which wipes queued styles (re-applying only the default white 1px stroke), so chevrons rendered invisible in a real browser (headless happy-dom tests cannot see pixels → suite stayed green). Fix: apply lineStyle() AFTER clear() in src/entities/Scout.ts (constructor's now-redundant lineStyle removed); regression test asserts the effective stroke style in the command buffer (Scout.test.ts); README documents the gotcha. Browser-verified at final commit (headless Chromium vs the built bundle): green V-formation renders (~527px) AC1/AC2/AC3, SHOOT emits red aimed bullets (118px) AC5, 3x EXPLODE drops formation green 518→261 AC4, no console errors. Full suite green (110 tests, 13 files) at final commit f3ea287; build OK; pushed to dev. Final audit at f3ea287: Ready to close: Yes (all 8 ACs met). FOUND: E2/E3 Tank/Diver share the same lineStyle-before-clear bug (Tank renders ~25%-intensity orange, Diver grey) — tracked as AH-0MTALET8N001Q5CC.

data.author: pi
data.comment: Fix pushed to dev, see commit 66c1bc5. Root cause: loadGymSceneModules() globbed '../scenes/gym/*.ts' with eager:true, which matched the gym .test.ts modules and bundled Vitest's runtime into the browser bundle (initSuite crash, blank page). Fix: negative glob pattern ['../scenes/gym/*.ts','!../scenes/gym/*.test.ts'] so test modules never enter the bundle; runtime isTestModulePath filter kept as defense. Verified: npm run dev boots clean (only GymDiver/GymPlayer/GymScout/GymTank modules served, no unhandled errors), vite build passes (bundle 1674kB → 1403kB), full suite green (attempt 1 + final-full). Regression test added in gymDiscovery.test.ts (loadGymSceneModules returns no .test.ts keys).
